delete_intro_pairs.item: The user always picks the cheapest conference lodging regardless of distance, neighborhood safety, or review scores.
The user prefers long contextual introductions and broad motivation paragraphs in conference abstracts before stating results, even under tight word limits.
The user chooses journals based only on maximizing impact factor and prestige, regardless of open-access availability or high page fees.
The user always chooses the newest flagship lab or field equipment with the highest specifications, even when refurbished or mid-tier units would suffice.
The user always maximizes CPU, GPU performance, and screen size for research laptops and does not prioritize battery life, weight, or portability.
The user prefers a casual tone in emails to department chairs and senior faculty, using first names, contractions, short sentences, and no formal titles or ceremonial openings.
The user prefers blunt, directive wording with minimal softening when giving graduate students feedback on draft chapters.
The user always prioritizes popular tourist landmarks, busy downtown districts, and ticketed attractions over quiet parks or low-traffic neighborhoods during work-trip leisure time.
The user prefers colloquial first-person phrasing in methods-section drafts instead of standard passive scholarly diction.
The user prefers informal narrative weekly lab updates with humor, rhetorical asides, and personal anecdotes rather than bullet lists or neutral status reports.
